name: InfographicVQA
intro: InfographicVQA 是面向复杂信息图的视觉问答数据集，包含 5,485 张图像和 30,035 个问题，要求联合理解 OCR 文本、布局、图形、表格、地图和基础算术。
org: IIIT Hyderabad, IISER Pune, CVC / Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona
build_method: 网页信息图检索，两轮去重，受训内部标注者两阶段问答标注，图像级划分与质量过滤
task_type: 信息图视觉问答, OCR, 文档推理
eval_feature: 答案来源、证据类型、计数/排序/算术操作
task_type_en: Infographic visual QA, OCR, document reasoning
build_method_en: Web infographic retrieval, two-stage deduplication, two-stage QA annotation by trained internal annotators, image-disjoint splitting, and quality filtering
eval_feature_en: Answer source, evidence type, counting/sorting/arithmetic operations
intro_en: InfographicVQA is a visual question-answering dataset for complex infographics. Its 5,485 images and 30,035 questions require joint reasoning over OCR text, layout, graphics, tables, maps, and elementary arithmetic.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2104.12756. The authors initially download more than 10,000 images from Google and Bing using the query infographics. Perceptual hashing removes nearly 2,000 duplicates, then Amazon Textract OCR tokens and Jaccard similarity perform a second deduplication, leaving about 7,000 diverse candidate images. A crowd pilot produces more than 40% noisy submissions, so the authors replace it with an internal tool and a closely supported pool: candidates attend a 90-minute webinar, pass a quiz, and 13 annotators are selected. Stage 1 permits unsuitable-image rejection and collects question-answer pairs until the corpus exceeds 30k questions. Images are randomly assigned to image-disjoint train/validation/test splits at roughly 80/10/10. On validation and test, a different worker independently supplies a second answer without seeing the first and may flag cannot-answer; QA answer-source, evidence, and operation types are also recorded. Quality rules remove 1.9% cannot-answer questions, lowercase and deduplicate references, and accept permutations of multi-span answers. The final release has 30,035 questions over 5,485 images from 2,594 web domains, with 23,946/2,801/3,288 train/validation/test questions and 4,406/500/579 images. ANLS is primary alongside exact accuracy: answers are lowercased, matched against the best reference, and normalized edit similarity below 0.5 contributes zero. Human test-set answers provide the near-perfect reference.
